summary:
The Florida Freeze Disaster Assistance Act (S. 4663, 119th Congress) is a single-purpose appropriations measure directing the Secretary of Agriculture to provide block grants to States for agricultural revenue losses attributable to freeze or cold weather conditions.

Section 1 supplies the short title. Section 2 constitutes the operative provision, appropriating $3,500,000,000 out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, as an additional amount under the "Agricultural Programs—Office of the Secretary" account. The appropriation is designated to remain available until expended (no-year funds), and is provided directly (an appropriation, not merely an authorization).

The funds are to be used by the Secretary to provide assistance in the form of block grants to States for losses of revenue, quality, or production of crops (including crops prevented from planting), trees, bushes, and vines, resulting from a freeze or cold weather condition.

The section imposes several conditions and provisos:

- The assistance "shall include" compensation to producers for losses of multi-year crops (a mandatory inclusion within the covered loss categories).
- Funds are made available "exclusively" for losses occurring in counties that received a disaster designation for freeze and related cold weather conditions issued by the Secretary on March 4, 2026. This date-specific and county-specific designation operates as a condition precedent limiting eligibility.
- Funds are made available upon the request of a State department of agriculture or other appropriate State agency, as determined by the Secretary, establishing a State-request mechanism as a condition of disbursement.
- A reporting requirement obligates the Secretary, not later than 120 days after the date of enactment and for each fiscal quarter thereafter until the amounts are expended, to submit reports to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations describing implementation.

Finally, the appropriated amount is designated by Congress as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 251(b)(2)(A)(i) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 (2 U.S.C. 901(b)(2)(A)(i)), a designation that has the effect of exempting the amount from applicable discretionary spending limits.

The bill contains no separate effective-date provision (thus taking effect upon enactment), no amendment to existing U.S. Code provisions, no sunset apart from the practical exhaustion of the no-year appropriation, and no separate authorization of appropriations distinct from the direct appropriation itself. The bill was introduced June 2, 2026, by Mr. Scott of Florida (for himself and Mrs. Moody) and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.
